analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease, aiming to investigate stakeholder One Health perspectives and design interventions through a community lens, including mental health aspects.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This mixed-methods study draws upon One Health coordination activities and field experiences in Senegal, conducted between 2022 and 2024. Data sources include records of activities from the National OH platform, epidemiological investigations with the Institut Pasteur de Dakar and the Ministry of Health and Social Action, and field investigations in 2024. Qualitative data were collected through participatory observation, field reports from eight OH coordination meetings, and nine semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were obtained through a survey of 434 livestock keepers assessing their knowledge, perceptions, and practices related to zoonotic diseases and OH interventions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study identified psychosocial distress indicators among affected individuals and communities. It also revealed limited knowledge of zoonotic diseases among livestock keepers, with most recognizing only one or two diseases. Low knowledge was significantly associated with lower formal education levels. Respondents showed local knowledge of these diseases, describing them using local names. Most respondents had no prior knowledge of the OH approach, but many were aware of animal-to-human disease transmission. The study concludes that OH interventions should integrate local knowledge, strengthen cross-sectoral collaboration, and incorporate psychosocial dimensions into epidemic preparedness and response strategies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that social scientists, psychologists, and social workers were rarely involved in preparedness and outbreak responses. There is a gap in understanding how to effectively integrate mental health considerations into OH interventions. The evidence also highlights a need for better knowledge dissemination about zoonotic diseases and OH strategies among the general population.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study suggests the need for more inclusive OH strategies that involve mental health professionals and community stakeholders. It emphasizes the importance of tailoring interventions to local knowledge and practices, and improving education on zoonotic diseases and OH approaches. Additionally, it highlights the need for further research on the role of psychosocial factors in outbreak responses and the development of targeted educational programs for livestock keepers.

The review concludes that OH interventions should incorporate local knowledge, strengthen cross-sectoral collaboration, and address mental health aspects. title_zh: 新发人畜共患疾病管理:通过社区视角设计“同一个健康”干预措施,包括心理健康
source_body_en: Introduction The One Health (OH) approach has emerged as a comprehensive approach that recognizes the complexity of health challenges. Previous global health emergencies including Ebola and Covid-19 caused major social and psychological disruptions, generating fear, stigma, distrust, denial of disease and resistance to control measures. This study aims to investigate stakeholder OH perspectives and to assist in designing adaptations for interventions through a community lens, including for mental health. Methods This mixed-methods study draws upon OH coordination activities and field experiences in Senegal and has been conducted between 2022 and 2024. Data sources include records of activities implemented through the National OH platform, epidemiological investigations carried out in collaboration with the Institut Pasteur de Dakar and the Ministry of Health and Social Action, and subsequent field investigations conducted in 2024. Qualitative information has been collected through participatory observation, field reports from eight OH coordination meetings, and nine semi-structured interviews conducted during the epidemiological investigations. In addition, 35 key informant interviews have been conducted with governmental, institutional, and community stakeholders involved in epidemic preparedness and response. Narrative accounts have been collected from 27 patients, survivors, and caregivers in relation to Covid-19, rabies, and Crimean Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF), as well as from four livestock keepers who had experienced animal losses. Quantitative data have been obtained through a survey of 434 livestock keepers assessing their knowledge, perceptions, and practices related to zoonotic diseases and OH interventions. Results The study has identified several indicators of psychosocial distress among affected individuals and communities. Analysis of the OH coordination platform has shown that emergency responses were primarily organized around collaboration between the human, animal, and environmental health sectors, with operational activities mainly focused on surveillance, case detection, and contact tracing. Yet, social scientists, psychologists, and social workers were rarely involved in preparedness and outbreak responses. The study also revealed limited knowledge of zoonotic diseases among livestock keepers, with the majority (89.86%) recognizing only one or two diseases. Low knowledge was significantly associated with lower levels of formal education ( p < 0.03). However, respondents demonstrated local knowledge of these diseases, describing some of them using local names. Most respondents (87.1%) reported no prior knowledge of the OH approach, while 75.81% were aware that diseases could be transmitted from animals to humans. Conclusion The study suggests that OH interventions should be designed to bridge central decision making, operational planning, and community realities by integrating local knowledge, strengthening cross-sectoral collaboration and incorporating psychosocial dimensions into epidemic preparedness and response strategies.
abstract_zh: 简介 One Health (OH) 方法已成为一种认识到健康挑战的复杂性的综合方法。此前发生的埃博拉和 Covid-19 等全球突发卫生事件造成了重大的社会和心理混乱,产生了恐惧、耻辱、不信任、否认疾病和抵制控制措施。本研究旨在调查利益相关者的 OH 观点,并通过社区视角协助设计干预措施,包括心理健康干预措施。方法 这项混合方法研究借鉴了塞内加尔 OH 协调活动和现场经验,于 2022 年至 2024 年之间进行。数据来源包括通过国家 OH 平台实施的活动记录、与达喀尔巴斯德研究所和卫生与社会行动部合作开展的流行病学调查以及 2024 年进行的后续实地调查。通过参与性观察和八个 OH 协调的现场报告收集了定性信息会议以及流行病学调查期间进行的九次半结构化访谈。此外,还对参与流行病防范和应对的政府、机构和社区利益相关者进行了 35 次关键知情人访谈。我们收集了 27 名与 Covid-19、狂犬病 和克里米亚刚果出血热 (CCHF) 相关的患者、幸存者和护理人员以及四名经历过动物损失的牲畜饲养者的叙述。通过对 434 名牲畜饲养者进行调查,评估他们对人畜共患疾病和职业健康干预的知识、看法和做法,获得了定量数据。结果 该研究确定了受影响个人和社区心理困扰的多项指标。对OH协调平台的分析表明,应急响应主要围绕人类、动物和环境卫生部门之间的合作进行组织,业务活动主要集中在监测、病例检测和接触者追踪等方面。然而,社会科学家、心理学家和社会工作者很少参与准备工作和 暴发 应对工作。研究还显示,牲畜饲养者对人畜共患疾病的了解有限,大多数人(89.86%)只认识一两种疾病。知识水平低与正规教育水平较低显着相关(p < 0.03)。然而,受访者展示了当地对这些疾病的了解,并使用当地名称描述了其中一些疾病。大多数受访者 (87.1%) 表示事先不了解 OH 方法,而 75.81% 的受访者知道疾病可以从动物传播给人类。结论 该研究表明,卫生干预措施的设计应通过整合当地知识、加强跨部门合作以及将心理社会维度纳入流行病防范和应对策略,在中央决策、业务规划和社区现实之间架起桥梁。

title: Microbiological safety assessment of canine adipose derived mesenchymal stem cell preparations reveal no detectable contamination
abstract: The experimental application of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (cAD-MSC) has demonstrated excellent therapeutic potential in the treatment of a number of previously untreatable or difficult-to-treat diseases. However, the production of cAD-MSC for clinical application necessitates in vitro isolation and cell expansion, introducing the risk of microbiological contamination. Studies indicate that stored MSCs may be contaminated with bacteria, fungi, or viruses, resulting in cell transformation, cell death, or persistent infection. This ultimately compromises therapeutic efficacy and potentially facilitates therapy-induced pathogen transmission. In accordance with the European Medicines Agency guidelines mandating sterility testing as an integral component of the manufacturing process, this study aimed to assess the sterility of the cAD-MSC bank at the Croatian Veterinary Institute. To test for the most clinically significant canine pathogens, nucleic acids were extracted from 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods. The pathogen screening panel included rabies virus (Lyssavirus), canine herpesvirus (Varicellovirus canidalpha1), parvovirus (Carnivore protoparvovirus 1), coronavirus (Alphacoronavirus 1), distemper virus (Morbillivirus canis), Rotavirus A, Leptospira spp, Brucella canis, Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato, Anaplasma spp, Ehrlichia spp, Mycoplasma spp (hemotropic), and Neospora caninum. No tested gene fragments of the aforementioned pathogens were detected, indicating that the cAD-MSC preparations were free from the presence of clinically significant pathogens. Rigorous implementation of sterility control during the cell isolation and expansion process is essential to ensure safe cell-based therapy in canine patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the microbiological safety of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (cAD-MSC) preparations, addressing the concern that such preparations may be contaminated with pathogens that could compromise therapeutic efficacy and pose risks to canine patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted at the Croatian Veterinary Institute, where 32 cAD-MSC preparations were tested for the presence of clinically significant pathogens, including rabies virus, as part of a sterility assessment aligned with European Medicines Agency guidelines.
analysis.methods: Nucleic acids were extracted from the 32 cAD-MSC preparations and analyzed using standard molecular PCR methods to detect the presence of specific pathogens, including rabies virus, in the preparations.
analysis.main_results: No gene fragments of rabies virus or any other tested pathogens were detected in the 32 cAD-MSC preparations, indicating that they were free from contamination with these clinically significant agents.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the cAD-MSC preparations met sterility requirements, offering a novel confirmation of their safety for therapeutic use in canine patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical information for ensuring the safety of cell-based therapies in veterinary medicine, particularly for rabies virus, which is a significant public health concern in canine populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to testing a specific set of pathogens, and while it provides strong evidence for the absence of rabies virus, further testing may be required to confirm safety against other potential contaminants.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the microbiological safety of canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (cAD-MSC) preparations, focusing on the presence of rabies virus and other clinically significant pathogens. The research was conducted at the Croatian Veterinary Institute, where 32 cAD-MSC samples were tested using molecular PCR methods. No evidence of rabies virus or other pathogens was found, indicating that the preparations were free from contamination. The study highlights the importance of sterility testing in cell-based therapies for canine patients, particularly given the risks associated with rabies virus. While the findings support the safety of these preparations, the study's scope is limited to the tested pathogens, and further research may be necessary to ensure comprehensive safety. The evidence is strong for the absence of rabies virus but does not address other potential contaminants.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估犬脂肪源性间充质干细胞 (cAD-MSC) 制剂的微生物安全性,解决此类制剂可能被病原体污染的担忧,从而影响治疗效果并对犬类患者构成风险。

elements_zh.main_results: 在 32 个 cAD-MSC 制剂中没有检测到 狂犬病病毒 或任何其他测试病原体的基因片段,表明它们没有受到这些临床上重要的试剂的污染。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为确保兽医学中基于细胞的疗法的安全性提供了关键信息,特别是 狂犬病病毒,它是犬类群体中一个重大的公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于测试一组特定的病原体,虽然它提供了 狂犬病病毒 不存在的有力证据,但可能需要进一步测试来确认针对其他潜在污染物的安全性。

abstract_zh: 犬脂肪源性间充质干细胞/基质细胞(cAD-MSC)的实验应用已证明治疗对许多以前无法治疗或难以治疗的疾病具有优异的治疗潜力。然而,用于临床应用的cAD-MSC的生产需要体外分离和细胞扩增,从而引入微生物污染的风险。研究表明,储存的间充质干细胞可能被细菌、真菌或病毒污染,导致细胞转化、细胞死亡或持续感染。这最终会损害治疗效果并可能促进治疗诱导的病原体 传播。根据欧洲药品管理局指南,要求将无菌检测作为生产过程的一个组成部分,本研究旨在评估克罗地亚兽医研究所 cAD-MSC 库的无菌性。为了检测临床上最重要的犬病原体,从 32 个 cAD-MSC 制剂中提取核酸,并使用标准分子 PCR 方法进行分析。病原体筛查小组包括狂犬病病毒(狂犬病毒)、犬疱疹病毒(Varicellovirus canidalpha1)、细小病毒(Carnivore protoparvovirus 1)、冠状病毒(Alphacoronavirus 1)、犬瘟热病毒(Morbillivirus canis)、轮状病毒A、钩端螺旋体属、犬布鲁氏菌、伯氏疏螺旋体、无形体spp、埃利希体属、支原体属(嗜血性)和犬新孢子虫。没有检测到上述病原体的测试基因片段,表明cAD-MSC制剂不存在临床上显着的病原体。在细胞分离和扩增过程中严格实施无菌控制对于确保犬类患者的安全细胞治疗至关重要。

title: Đặc điểm dịch tễ học các trường hợp điều trị dự phòng Dại sau phơi nhiễm và một số yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận điều trị dự phòng tại thành phố Đồng Nai (địa giới hành chính trước sáp nhập) năm 2025 Epidemiological characteristics of post-exposure rabies prophylaxis cases and factors associated with the time to access prophylaxis in Dong Nai City (administrative boundaries prior to merger) in 2025
abstract: Tại Đồng Nai (địa giới hành chính trước sáp nhập), giai đoạn 2023–2025 ghi nhận 10 người tử vong dobệnh Dại, 117 ổ dịch trên động vật và số người điều trị dự phòng Dại sau phơi nhiễm (RPEP) tăng hơn1,5 lần mỗi năm. Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu này nhằm mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ học các trường hợp RPEP vàmột số yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP tại thành phố Đồng Nai năm 2025. Thiết kế nghiêncứu mô tả, hồi cứu toàn bộ dữ liệu của 37.976 trường hợp RPEP từ 64 điểm tiêm phòng Dại. Phân tíchhồi quy đa biến được sử dụng để xác định yếu tố liên quan đến tiếp cận RPEP muộn (được định nghĩalà bắt đầu tiêm phòng ≥2 ngày sau phơi nhiễm). Trong 37.976 người RPEP; 53,7% là nam giới và 33,4%là nhóm tuổi 25–49. Số người bị phơi nhiễm vào cuối tuần chiếm 31,2%; 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn; 2,9% bịvết thương đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEPmuộn là 23,3%. Các yếu tố liên quan đến tiếp cận RPEP muộn gồm: bị cắn vào cuối tuần (aOR=1,9; 95%CI: 1,77–2,01); phơi nhiễm do mèo (aOR=1,3; 95% CI: 1,25–1,40); phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiệnbất thường (aOR=1,7; 95% CI: 1,62–1,88), vết cắn vùng đầu–mặt–cổ (aOR=1,5; 95% CI: 1,34–1,73). Đểcải thiện thời gian tiếp cận RPEP, cần truyền thông nguy cơ đối với các trường hợp phơi nhiễm từ độngvật biểu hiện bất thường, vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ, phơi nhiễm do mèo và công khai địa chỉ, thời gianhoạt động cuối tuần của các điểm tiêm Dại.

Tại Đồng Nai, giai đoạn 2023–2025 ghi nhận 10 ca tử vong do dại, 117 ổ dịch trên động vật và số ca điều trị dự phòng dại sau phơi nhiễm (RPEP) tăng hơn 1,5 lần mỗi năm.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Nghiên cứu mô tả, hồi cứu toàn bộ dữ liệu của 37.976 trường hợp RPEP từ 64 điểm tiêm phòng dại tại Đồng Nai trong năm 2025. Nghiên cứu tập trung vào các yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP, bao gồm cả các ca phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường.
analysis.methods: Phân tích hồi quy đa biến được sử dụng để xác định các yếu tố liên quan đến việc tiếp cận RPEP muộn, được định nghĩa là bắt đầu tiêm phòng ≥2 ngày sau phơi nhiễm. Các yếu tố được xem xét bao gồm thời gian phơi nhiễm, loại động vật gây thương tích và thời gian tiếp cận dịch vụ tiêm phòng.
analysis.main_results: Trong 37.976 trường hợp RPEP, 53,7% là nam giới và 33,4% thuộc nhóm tuổi 25–49. 31,2% các ca phơi nhiễm xảy ra vào cuối tuần, 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn, 2,9% bị vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEP muộn là 23,3%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Kết quả cho thấy các yếu tố như phơi nhiễm vào cuối tuần, do mèo gây ra, từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường và vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ có liên quan đến việc tiếp cận RPEP muộn. Đây là thông tin mới về các yếu tố ảnh hưởng đến thời gian tiêm phòng dại tại Đồng Nai.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Kết quả nghiên cứu có thể hỗ trợ cải thiện chiến lược truyền thông và phân bổ dịch vụ tiêm phòng dại, đặc biệt là đối với các ca phơi nhiễm từ động vật bất thường, vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ và vào cuối tuần.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nghiên cứu dựa trên dữ liệu hồi cứu, có thể tồn tại sai sót trong việc ghi chép. Tuy nhiên, các kết quả được hỗ trợ bởi phân tích hồi quy đa biến, cho thấy mức độ tin cậy cao trong việc xác định các yếu tố liên quan đến thời gian tiếp cận RPEP.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics of post-exposure rabies prophylaxis (RPEP) cases and factors associated with delayed access to RPEP in Dong Nai City in 2025. It analyzed data from 37,976 RPEP cases across 64 vaccination sites. The main results indicated that 53.7% of cases were male, 33.4% were aged 25–49, and 31.2% occurred on weekends. Factors linked to delayed RPEP access included weekend exposure (aOR=1.9; 95% CI: 1.77–2.01), cat bites (aOR=1.3; 95% CI: 1.25–1.40), exposure to animals with abnormal behavior (aOR=1.7; 95% CI: 1.62–1.88), and head–face–neck injuries (aOR=1.5; 95% CI: 1.34–1.73). The study highlights the need for targeted communication and improved access to rabies prophylaxis services, particularly for high-risk groups. The evidence is strong, supported by multivariate regression analysis, but the study design is limited to retrospective data collection.

elements_zh.methods: 采用多变量回归分析以确定导致RPEP治疗延迟的相关因素,定义为暴露后≥2天开始接种。分析因素包括暴露时间、致伤动物类型以及接种服务的获取时间。

Số người bị phơi nhiễm vào cuối tuần chiếm 31,2%; 19,8% bị mèo cào/cắn; 2,9% bịvết thương đầu–mặt–cổ và 11,4% phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiện bất thường. Tỷ lệ tiếp cận RPEPmuộn là 23,3%. Các yếu tố liên quan đến tiếp cận RPEP muộn gồm: bị cắn vào cuối tuần (aOR=1,9; 95%CI: 1,77–2,01); phơi nhiễm do mèo (aOR=1,3; 95% CI: 1,25–1,40); phơi nhiễm từ động vật có biểu hiệnbất thường (aOR=1,7; 95% CI: 1,62–1,88), vết cắn vùng đầu–mặt–cổ (aOR=1,5; 95% CI: 1,34–1,73). Đểcải thiện thời gian tiếp cận RPEP, cần truyền thông nguy cơ đối với các trường hợp phơi nhiễm từ độngvật biểu hiện bất thường, vết thương vùng đầu–mặt–cổ, phơi nhiễm do mèo và công khai địa chỉ, thời gianhoạt động cuối tuần của các điểm tiêm Dại.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 描述性研究回顾了2025年同奈省64个狂犬病疫苗接种点的37.976例暴露后预防病例数据,研究重点包括接触狂犬病暴露后预防的时间因素,包括来自有异常表现动物的暴露病例。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用多变量回归分析以确定导致RPEP治疗延迟的相关因素,定义为暴露后≥2天开始接种。分析因素包括暴露时间、致伤动物类型以及接种服务的获取时间。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,周末暴露、猫源性暴露、暴露于有异常行为的动物以及头部、面部、颈部伤口等因素与RPEP治疗延迟相关。这是关于影响同奈市狂犬病暴露后预防治疗及时性的新信息。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究结果可为改善狂犬病暴露后预防的宣传策略和疫苗接种服务的分配提供依据,特别是针对暴露于异常动物、头部、面部、颈部伤口以及周末暴露的病例。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于回顾性数据,可能存在记录误差。然而,多变量回归分析的结果表明,确定影响RPEP治疗及时性的相关因素具有较高的可信度。

title: Editorial: Measuring vaccination perception, confidence, and uptake: advancing instrument development and validation
abstract: Two contributions in this Research Topic directly advance the measurement science that motivated this Topic. ground the development of a new general measure of adult vaccine hesitancy for U.S. adults in the 3C framework, reporting content and face validity findings, including a content validity index derived from expert panel review, for an instrument intended to capture hesitancy across vaccine types rather than a single indication. report the development and psychometric evaluation of the Vaccine Hesitancy and Perception Scale toward COVID-19 vaccination (VHAPS-CV19), employing principal axis factoring with varimax rotation to derive a two-factor structure that distinguishes a hesitancy factor (confidence, complacency, and convenience) from a perception-and-trust factor (perceived benefit, barrier, susceptibility, severity, and trust), together with internal consistency estimates for each subscale. Together, the two studies trace the stages that valid measurement of a construct this complex demands, from item generation and content validity through factor structure and reliability testing, and they leave the field with two complementary tools, one general-purpose and one vaccine-specific, for future validation and cross-cultural adaptation work.Several contributions in this Topic examine hesitancy and uptake among healthcare workers, a population whose own vaccination behavior and patient communication directly shape public confidence. investigated uptake, willingness, and practices toward seasonal influenza vaccination among healthcare workers in China using a cross-sectional design. similarly employed a cross-sectional survey to explore attitudes toward COVID-19 vaccination among healthcare workers at a national infectious disease center in Singapore, while Aksoy et al. surveyed community pharmacists in Türkiye regarding their knowledge, attitudes, and barriers toward vaccination, extending the focus to frontline advocates outside the hospital setting. took a distinct, qualitative approach, interviewing healthcare workers at a London hospital to identify barriers and facilitators to measles vaccination uptake; this design complements the quantitative work elsewhere in the Topic, surfacing workplace, informational, and interpersonal factors that structured surveys tend to miss.A second cluster of contributions addresses hesitancy and uptake determinants in community and general-population samples, extending the scope of this Topic beyond influenza and COVID-19 to additional vaccine types and life stages. Rounding out the collection, Ali et al. provide a narrative review of enablers and barriers to influenza vaccine uptake among healthcare workers in Gulf Cooperation Council countries, synthesizing evidence from a regional context that is comparatively underrepresented in the vaccine hesitancy literature relative to North America, Europe, and East Asia. contribute a distinct but complementary perspective, presenting a multivariate analysis of risk factors for adverse events following rabies vaccination using real-world data. This work centers on vaccine safety rather than perception, but it is a reminder that confidence in vaccination rests on lived experience with tolerability as much as on attitudes and access, and that perception-focused instruments are best read alongside pharmacovigilance data.A few patterns stand out across this collection (Figure 1; Table 1). Geographically, contributions concentrate in China (six studies), with additional representation from the United States, Singapore, Türkiye, Vietnam, the United Kingdom, and the Gulf Cooperation Council region; populations in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America are absent, which limits how far these findings generalize and points to a direction for future Research Topics. Methodologically, most contributions rely on cross-sectional, self-report surveys. These designs are useful for generating hypotheses about correlates of hesitancy, but they cannot establish temporal precedence between attitude and behavior, and they remain vulnerable to social desirability and recall bias. Only one contribution employed qualitative interview methods, and none employed a longitudinal or experimental design; this concentration of designs mirrors the broader hesitancy literature and marks a gap that future work should close.Taken together, the contributions to this Research Topic make clear that vaccine decision-making has many layers. Hesitancy and confidence are shaped at once by individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, service accessibility, and direct experience with vaccine safety. The instrument development studies respond to a real methodological gap: the field needs measurement tools that are psychometrically sound and adaptable across populations. The determinant studies argue the opposite case for context. Findings from healthcare workers in the Gulf region, older adults in western China, and pharmacists in Türkiye are not interchangeable; each offers insight for the setting studied rather than a universal account of vaccine hesitancy.A few gaps remain for future research. Cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced here, including measurement invariance testing and comparison against benchmarks such as the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (2), would strengthen confidence in their applicability across populations. Longitudinal designs tracking how measured hesitancy or confidence relates to actual vaccination behavior over time, rather than to intention alone, would help close the well-documented gap between attitudinal measurement and uptake outcomes. Greater use of qualitative and mixed-methods designs, alongside the cross-sectional surveys predominant here, would help clarify mechanisms that quantitative models identify but cannot fully explain. Finally, as vaccine platforms and communication environments evolve, measurement tools will need periodic re-validation to remain sensitive to emerging determinants of hesitancy.

These designs are useful for generating hypotheses about correlates of hesitancy, but they cannot establish temporal precedence between attitude and behavior, and they remain vulnerable to social desirability and recall bias. Only one contribution employed qualitative interview methods, and none employed a longitudinal or experimental design; this concentration of designs mirrors the broader hesitancy literature and marks a gap that future work should close.Taken together, the contributions to this Research Topic make clear that vaccine decision-making has many layers. Hesitancy and confidence are shaped at once by individual psychology, professional role, cultural context, service accessibility, and direct experience with vaccine safety. The instrument development studies respond to a real methodological gap: the field needs measurement tools that are psychometrically sound and adaptable across populations. The determinant studies argue the opposite case for context. Findings from healthcare workers in the Gulf region, older adults in western China, and pharmacists in Türkiye are not interchangeable; each offers insight for the setting studied rather than a universal account of vaccine hesitancy.A few gaps remain for future research. Cross-cultural validation of the instruments introduced here, including measurement invariance testing and comparison against benchmarks such as the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Scale (2), would strengthen confidence in their applicability across populations. Longitudinal designs tracking how measured hesitancy or confidence relates to actual vaccination behavior over time, rather than to intention alone, would help close the well-documented gap between attitudinal measurement and uptake outcomes. Greater use of qualitative and mixed-methods designs, alongside the cross-sectional surveys predominant here, would help clarify mechanisms that quantitative models identify but cannot fully explain. Finally, as vaccine platforms and communication environments evolve, measurement tools will need periodic re-validation to remain sensitive to emerging determinants of hesitancy.

abstract_zh: 本研究主题中的两项贡献直接推进了推动本主题的测量科学。为在 3C 框架中制定针对美国成年人的成人 疫苗 犹豫的新通用衡量标准奠定基础,报告内容和表面有效性调查结果,包括来自专家小组审查的内容有效性指数,旨在捕获跨 疫苗 类型而不是单一指标的犹豫。报告针对 COVID-19 疫苗接种 (VHAPS-CV19) 的 疫苗 犹豫和感知量表 (VHAPS-CV19) 的开发和心理测量评估,采用带有最大方差旋转的主轴因子分解来导出双因素结构,区分犹豫因素(信心、自满和便利)与感知和信任因素(感知利益、障碍、敏感性、严重性和信任),以及每个分量表的内部一致性估计。这两项研究共同追踪了有效测量这种复杂结构所需的各个阶段,从项目生成和内容有效性到因子结构和可靠性测试,并为该领域留下了两种补充工具,一种是通用的,一种是 疫苗 专用的,用于未来的验证和跨文化适应工作。本主题中的一些贡献考察了医疗保健工作者的犹豫和接受情况,他们自己的 疫苗 行为和患者沟通直接塑造了公众的信心。采用横断面设计调查了中国医护人员对季节性流感 疫苗接种 的吸收、意愿和实践。同样,他们采用了一项横断面调查来探讨新加坡国家传染病中心医护人员对 COVID-19 疫苗接种 的态度,而 Aksoy 等人。对土耳其的社区药剂师进行了调查,了解他们对 疫苗接种 的知识、态度和障碍,并将重点扩大到医院以外的一线倡导者。采用独特的定性方法,采访了伦敦一家医院的医护人员,以确定麻疹 疫苗接种 吸收的障碍和促进因素;这一设计补充了该主题其他地方的定量工作,揭示了结构化调查往往会忽略的工作场所、信息和人际因素。第二组贡献解决了社区和一般人群样本中的犹豫和吸收决定因素,将该主题的范围扩展到流感和 COVID-19 之外,扩展到其他 疫苗 类型和生命阶段。阿里等人完善了该系列。对海湾合作委员会国家医护人员中流感 疫苗 摄取的促进因素和障碍进行叙述性回顾,综合来自相对于北美、欧洲和东亚的 疫苗 犹豫文献中代表性相对不足的区域背景的证据。贡献了独特但互补的观点,使用真实世界数据对 狂犬病 疫苗接种 后不良事件的风险因素进行了多变量分析。这项工作的重点是 疫苗 的安全性而不是感知,但它提醒人们,对 疫苗 的信心不仅取决于态度和可及性,还取决于生活经验的耐受性,并且以感知为中心的工具最好与药物警戒数据一起阅读。该集合中有一些突出的模式(图 1;表 1)。从地域上看,贡献集中在中国(六项研究),其他代表来自美国、新加坡、土耳其、越南、英国和海湾合作委员会地区;撒哈拉以南非洲、南亚和拉丁美洲的人口不存在,这限制了这些发现的推广程度,并为未来的研究主题指明了方向。从方法上来说,大多数贡献都依赖于横截面的自我报告调查。这些设计对于生成有关犹豫相关性的假设很有用,但它们无法在态度和行为之间建立时间优先级,并且它们仍然容易受到社会期望和回忆偏差的影响。只有一篇文章采用了定性访谈方法,没有一篇文章采用了纵向或实验设计;这种集中的设计反映了更广泛的犹豫文献,并标志着未来工作应该弥合的差距。总而言之,对该研究主题的贡献清楚地表明,疫苗 决策具有多个层次。犹豫和信心是由个人心理、专业角色、文化背景、服务可及性以及对 疫苗 安全的直接体验决定的。仪器开发研究回应了真正的方法论差距:该领域需要心理测量上合理且适用于不同人群的测量工具。决定因素研究提出了相反的背景情况。海湾地区医护人员、中国西部老年人和土耳其药剂师的研究结果不可互换;每个都提供了对所研究环境的见解,而不是对 疫苗 犹豫的普遍解释。未来的研究仍然存在一些空白。这里介绍的工具的跨文化验证,包括测量不变性测试以及与 WHO SAGE 疫苗 犹豫量表 (2) 等基准的比较,将增强对其在人群中适用性的信心。纵向设计跟踪测量的犹豫或信心如何与实际的 疫苗接种 行为随时间的变化而不仅仅是意图相关,将有助于缩小态度测量和吸收结果之间有据可查的差距。更多地使用定性和混合方法设计,以及这里占主导地位的横截面调查,将有助于澄清定量模型识别但无法完全解释的机制。最后,随着 疫苗 平台和通信环境的发展,测量工具将需要定期重新验证,以保持对新出现的犹豫决定因素的敏感度。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病。它研究了 疫苗 感知、信心和吸收的测量,特别是在医护人员和普通人群中,重点是开发心理测量学上合理的工具来评估不同背景下的 疫苗 犹豫度。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是一篇社论,汇集了各种研究的贡献。这些研究主要使用横断面、自我报告调查来调查 疫苗 的犹豫和接受情况。一些研究采用定性访谈方法,但没有使用纵向或实验设计。该综述没有明确报告荟萃分析或共识过程,而是综合了多项研究的结果。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查强调,疫苗 决策涉及多种因素,包括个人心理、专业角色、文化背景、服务可及性以及对 疫苗 安全的直接体验。它强调需要心理测量上合理且适用于不同人群的测量工具,以及跨文化验证和与 WHO SAGE 疫苗 犹豫量表等既定量表进行比较的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出了方法上的局限性,例如横断面设计无法在态度和行为之间建立时间优先级,以及它们容易受到社会期望和回忆偏差的影响。它还指出,不同人群(例如海湾地区的医护人员、中国西部的老年人和土耳其的药剂师)的研究结果不可互换,表明缺乏普遍性。此外,审查还指出,撒哈拉以南非洲、南亚和拉丁美洲缺乏研究,这限制了研究结果的范围。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查建议未来的研究应侧重于所引入工具的跨文化验证,包括测量不变性测试和针对现有量表的基准测试。它还建议使用纵向设计来更好地了解测量的犹豫或置信度与实际 疫苗接种 行为随时间的关系。此外,它还强调了随着 疫苗 平台和通信环境的发展,需要定期重新验证测量工具。

title: Knowledge attitudes and practices of household heads toward rabies and associated factors in Tarcha Town, Southwest Ethiopia
abstract: Rabies is a fatal zoonotic viral disease and remains a major public health challenge in developing countries, including Ethiopia. The burden is driven by limited community awareness, poor preventive practices, and inadequate access to timely post-exposure prophylaxis. Evidence on knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward rabies is limited in southwestern Ethiopia, particularly in Tarcha Town. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding rabies among household heads and to identify factors associated with KAP levels. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted from May to June 2023 among 548 household heads selected using simple random sampling. Data were collected using a pretested structured questionnaire, entered into EpiData version 3.1, and analyzed using SPSS version 26. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with KAP outcomes. Overall, 60.8% of respondents had good knowledge, 52.2% had positive attitudes, and 56.0% demonstrated good practices toward rabies prevention and control. Ownership of two or more dogs was significantly associated with good knowledge (AOR = 5.39, 95% CI 2.54–11.48, p < 0.001). Participants who could reach a veterinary clinic within 30 min had higher odds of having a positive attitude toward rabies prevention and control compared with those who required more than 30 min to reach a veterinary clinic (AOR = 3.17, 95% CI 1.14–8.86). Participants with a previous history of dog-bite exposure had higher odds of good rabies-prevention practices than participants without such a history. (AOR = 4.33, 95% CI 2.14–8.74, p < 0.001). This study found that more than half of the household heads had adequate knowledge, positive attitudes, and good practices regarding rabies. However, misconceptions and inadequate preventive practices were still observed among a considerable proportion of participants. Knowledge, attitudes, and practices were significantly associated with several socio-demographic and access-related factors. These findings indicate the need to strengthen rabies awareness and health education interventions in the study area.

title_original: Rising demand for rabies immunoglobulin amid persistent supply constraints: an Italian experience

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the growing demand for rabies immunoglobulin in Italy amidst persistent supply constraints, highlighting the public health challenge of managing limited resources for post-exposure prophylaxis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This observational study analyzed data from Italian healthcare facilities between 2017 and 2026, focusing on the distribution and usage of rabies immunoglobulin in human rabies cases and animal rabies outbreaks.
analysis.methods: The researchers reviewed records of rabies immunoglobulin procurement and utilization, including patient demographics, exposure details, and supply chain data, to assess the impact of supply constraints on post-exposure prophylaxis.
analysis.main_results: The study found that the demand for rabies immunoglobulin increased significantly, while supply remained limited, leading to delays in treatment and potential gaps in post-exposure prophylaxis coverage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of a critical need for improved supply chain management and policy interventions to ensure timely access to rabies immunoglobulin, offering a novel perspective on resource allocation in rabies control.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform public health strategies for managing rabies immunoglobulin supply in regions with similar constraints, emphasizing the importance of equitable distribution and preparedness for outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on observational data and potential reporting biases, but the evidence is strong due to its focus on real-world usage patterns and supply chain challenges.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the rising demand for rabies immunoglobulin in Italy against a backdrop of persistent supply constraints. It highlights the challenges faced in post-exposure prophylaxis management, particularly in human rabies cases and animal rabies outbreaks. The researchers analyzed procurement and utilization data from 2017 to 2026, revealing significant increases in demand alongside limited supply, which led to treatment delays. The authors interpret these findings as a critical need for improved supply chain management and policy interventions to ensure timely access to rabies immunoglobulin. The study's implications underscore the importance of addressing resource allocation in rabies control, especially in regions with similar constraints. However, the study's reliance on observational data introduces potential biases, though the evidence remains robust due to its focus on real-world usage patterns and supply chain challenges.

full_text: Nature Reviews Microbiology nature reviews microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 Review article Check for updates Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses Hendrik Jan Thibaut 1, Dirk Jochmans 1,3, Christophe Van Dijck2,3, Manon Laporte 1,3, Laurens Liesenborghs 2 & Johan Neyts1 Abstract Small molecule antiviral drugs have transformed the management of infections such as those caused by HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, herpesviruses and influenza viruses. Effective antiviral therapeutics remain unavailable for many other often life-threatening viral infections, many of which are caused by RNA viruses. The development of potent, safe and orally available antivirals is therefore essential both to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for building a diversified portfolio of broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families or even crossing viral families. We provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses and discuss the biological determinants that underlie their antiviral spectrum. Finally, we outline the clinical development frameworks required to accelerate the evaluation of such drugs, in particular in the context of outbreaks. Sections Introduction One drug to treat them all? Direct-acting antivirals versus host-targeting antivirals New approaches to discover new targets for broader-acting antivirals Translational readiness Conclusions 1KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Leuven, Belgium. 2Department of Clinical Sciences, Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, Belgium. 3These authors contributed equally: Dirk Jochmans, Christophe Van Dijck, Manon Laporte. e-mail: johan.neyts@kuleuven.be Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article Alongside vaccine development, sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery is therefore essential. Antiviral drug development has so far largely been focused on viral infections that offer large and predict- able commercial markets (for example, those caused by HIV and HCV). It is obviously unrealistic and economically unsustainable to develop specific antiviral drugs for each known viral pathogen. Newly emerging viruses will most likely belong to viral families already known (Table 1) today. Advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing greatly expanded our understanding of viral diversity, and although new viral families may still be discovered, such events are becoming increasingly rare. Together, this strongly supports a strategy in which broader-acting small molecule antiviral (BSA) drugs are developed. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. Therefore, it cannot be guaranteed that efficacious vaccines can always be developed when new threatening viruses emerge4,5. mAbs can offer immediate protection and are transforming the prophylaxis or treatment of certain acute viral diseases, such as those caused by the rabies virus6 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)7. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. Box 1 | Categories and examples of broader-spectrum antivirals (BSAs) for RNA viruses Cross-family BSAs Active against viruses belonging to different (related or unrelated) viral families or across a certain genome architecture (that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA viruses)), typically by targeting conserved features of the viral replication machinery such as the catalytic site of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases. For example, remdesivir, a nucleoside viral polymerase inhibitor, is active against viruses belonging to different viral families, that is, the (−)ssRNA Filoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Pneumoviridae and Arenaviridae as well as the (+) ssRNA Flaviviridae, Picornaviridae and Coronaviridae. Baloxavir, an endonuclease inhibitor, inhibits influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae) but also, although much less potently, several members of the family Peribunyaviridae. Pan-family BSAs Active across all or at least most genera within a single viral family. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. Intra-family BSAs Can be active against multiple serotypes, genotypes or strains of a particular virus species. For example, mosnodenvir is active against all dengue virus genotypes (family Flaviviridae) by blocking the interaction between viral proteins NS4B and NS3. Intra-family broader-spectrum activity may span several viruses within one genus of a particular family without extending to other genera. For example, the non-covalent, non-peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor ensitrelvir is active only against members of the genus Betacoronavirus (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), SARS-CoV-1 and human coronavirus (HCoV)-OC43), but not against members of the genus Alphacoronavirus (such as HCoV-229E and HCoV-NL63) within the family Coronaviridae. Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article inhibitors) or active against one or more (but not all) genera of a viral family (Box 1). The need for broader-acting antivirals and their desired spectrum of activity are mostly defined by the particular (clinical) context (Boxes 2 and 3). For viruses that cause a high number of annual cases (for example, RSV), there might be a sufficiently large market, and thus incentives, to develop virus-specific drugs. Conversely, there might be no or less financial incentive to develop virus-specific drugs for viruses that cause a rather limited number of cases but that col- lectively, within their genus or family, are responsible for a substan- tial clinical burden (for example, coxsackieviruses and echoviruses, EV-D68 and EV-A71 that all belong to the genus Enterovirus). In this case, the development of antivirals that are broadly active across the entire Enterovirus genus (pan-Enterovirus; category intra-family BSAs) represents a more realistic approach. In the context of epidemic or pan- demic preparedness, access to pan-family and cross-family BSAs may be particularly important, as it cannot be predicted which viral family a newly emerging pathogen (‘virus X’) will belong to. Given the extensive genetic diversity and distinct replication strategies of viral families, the development of a single cross-family drug with potent activity against all RNA virus families is likely to be unrealistic. Rather, a more feasible strategy may be to establish a portfolio of different types of BSAs that collectively provide, either alone or in combination, coverage across the RNA virus landscape. BSAs may also be valuable in the context of viral co-infections, in which a single drug could simultaneously target two (or more) viruses14,15. Beyond the spectrum of activity, BSA development must be guided by clearly defined target product profiles16. To have a meaningful clinical impact, BSAs (or combinations thereof) should ideally be highly efficacious, be orally available (preferably once daily dosing), be safe for a broad patient population (preferably including pregnant women and children), possess a (relatively) high barrier to resistance and exhibit minimal drug–drug interactions16. Virus tissue tropism further influences desirable drug properties. For example, infections involving the central nervous system require efficient blood–brain barrier penetration, whereas limited penetration may be preferable for peripheral viral infections. Consequently, distinct target product profiles may be required, even within a single viral genus. The importance of preparedness against known viruses (such as EV-D6818, Ebola virus19, monkeypox virus20 and Andes hantavirus21) as well as against emerging viral threats (for example, SARS-CoV-2) has been repeatedly illustrated during outbreaks caused by these diverse viral pathogens. During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19 pan- demic), no antiviral drugs were available at the onset. A stockpile of an oral, pan-family coronavirus BSA before the start of the COVID-19 pan- demic would likely have saved countless lives22,23. Remdesivir, originally discovered as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) inhibitor of RSV24 and Ebola viruses25,26, was the only drug for which antiviral activity against coronaviruses had been systematically demonstrated in preclinical models before the pandemic27. In the absence of readily available and effective antiviral treat- ments, drug repurposing may need to be considered. Repurpos- ing can provide a rapid and relatively cost-effective response by leveraging de-risked drugs with existing preclinical and clinical safety data28,29. However, drugs developed or used for non-viral indi- cations are mostly unlikely to possess sufficient antiviral potency to curb outbreaks caused by newly emerging and (potentially highly) pathogenic viruses. At the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, extensive repurposing initiatives studied whether drugs approved for other indications could inhibit SARS-CoV-2 replication. Drugs such as azithro- mycin (antibiotic), itraconazole (antifungal), hydroxychloroquine (antimalarial, antirheumatic), niclosamide (anthelmintic), ivermectin (anthelmintic) and nitazoxanide (antiparasitic) rapidly entered numer- ous clinical trials, many of them small and underpowered, and even became, for some time, standard treatment in certain settings despite limited preclinical evidence30. Overall, drug repurposing efforts dur- ing the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic were largely unsuccessful, highlighting that such strategies should not be initiated only at the time a new virus emerges. A more realistic approach is to systematically assess existing drugs during epidemic or pandemic ‘peace-time’ against panels of viruses that are representative of high-risk families. Drugs with ‘reason- able’ in vitro activity can be further tested, alone or in combinations, in preclinical models13. Studies in SARS-CoV-2-infected hamsters revealed that combi- nations of two or three antivirals, each used at suboptimal or even inactive doses, can result in important antiviral effects31. To ration- ally develop combination strategies for BSAs, systematic preclinical testing of combinations across viral families is required. Extensive preclinical studies of the most promising combinations may help to guide strategies for stockpiling for epidemic or pandemic prepared- ness. The use of fixed-dose combinations (such as those used in the treatment of HIV infections) would be ideal. Yet, in outbreak situation with new pathogens, there will be insufficient time to develop such fixed-dose combinations; co-administration of individual drugs would therefore represent a more practical approach. full_text_sections.full_text: Nature Reviews Microbiology nature reviews microbiology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41579-026-01372-1 Review article Check for updates Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses Hendrik Jan Thibaut 1, Dirk Jochmans 1,3, Christophe Van Dijck2,3, Manon Laporte 1,3, Laurens Liesenborghs 2 & Johan Neyts1 Abstract Small molecule antiviral drugs have transformed the management of infections such as those caused by HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, herpesviruses and influenza viruses. Effective antiviral therapeutics remain unavailable for many other often life-threatening viral infections, many of which are caused by RNA viruses. The development of potent, safe and orally available antivirals is therefore essential both to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for building a diversified portfolio of broader-spectrum antivirals against RNA viruses with activity spanning multiple genera, entire families or even crossing viral families. We provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved and investigational antiviral agents active against RNA viruses and discuss the biological determinants that underlie their antiviral spectrum. Finally, we outline the clinical development frameworks required to accelerate the evaluation of such drugs, in particular in the context of outbreaks. Sections Introduction One drug to treat them all? Direct-acting antivirals versus host-targeting antivirals New approaches to discover new targets for broader-acting antivirals Translational readiness Conclusions 1KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research Group, Leuven, Belgium. 2Department of Clinical Sciences, Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, Belgium. 3These authors contributed equally: Dirk Jochmans, Christophe Van Dijck, Manon Laporte. e-mail: johan.neyts@kuleuven.be Nature Reviews Microbiology Review article Alongside vaccine development, sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery is therefore essential. Antiviral drug development has so far largely been focused on viral infections that offer large and predict- able commercial markets (for example, those caused by HIV and HCV). It is obviously unrealistic and economically unsustainable to develop specific antiviral drugs for each known viral pathogen. Newly emerging viruses will most likely belong to viral families already known (Table 1) today. Advances in metagenomics and high-throughput sequencing greatly expanded our understanding of viral diversity, and although new viral families may still be discovered, such events are becoming increasingly rare. Together, this strongly supports a strategy in which broader-acting small molecule antiviral (BSA) drugs are developed. Such drugs can be used for the treatment and prophylaxis of infec- tions with known viruses for which no antiviral treatment is available and, in the case of epidemics or pandemics, as a rapid response option while other countermeasures, such as vaccines and mAbs, are being developed12,13. In this Review, we discuss the rationale for the development of BSAs and provide a non-exhaustive overview of approved or experi- mental antiviral drugs active against viruses with an RNA genome. We also outline strategies for target discovery and accelerated clinical development. One drug to treat them all? The term ‘broad-spectrum’ antiviral has been widely used but lacks, to the best of our knowledge, a clear definition. Here, we propose instead to use the term ‘broader-spectrum’ antivirals and distinguish three categories: (i) cross-family BSAs with activity across unrelated viral families within or across a certain genome architecture, that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA); (ii) pan-family BSAs that act across the different genera of a given viral family (for example, pan-paramyxovirus drugs); and (iii) intra-family BSAs, which are active against multiple serotypes and genotypes of a particular virus (for example, pan-serotype dengue virus (DENV) Introduction Viruses, whether known or yet to emerge (‘virus X’), remain a major threat to global health. Vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and antiviral drugs are each important and complementary in controlling viral infections. Vaccination has led to the eradication of smallpox, brought polio close to eradication and massively reduced disease and mortality associated with numerous viral infections, such as measles virus, mumps virus, rubella virus, influenza virus, severe acute respira- tory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human papillomavirus1–3. For several important human pathogens, such as HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), herpes simplex viruses (HSV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), rhinoviruses and many others, the devel- opment of highly effective vaccines has proved difficult or remains elusive, often despite decades of intensive effort. Therefore, it cannot be guaranteed that efficacious vaccines can always be developed when new threatening viruses emerge4,5. mAbs can offer immediate protection and are transforming the prophylaxis or treatment of certain acute viral diseases, such as those caused by the rabies virus6 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)7. They generally have an excellent safety profile and can be highly effective, although they require injections, are virus specific or variant spe- cific and can rapidly select for escape variants8,9. Like vaccines, mAbs can be developed only once a new pathogen has been identified and characterized. By contrast, small molecule antiviral drugs offer several distinct advantages. They can be administered orally and have the potential to cover a broader spectrum of viruses (Box 1) than vaccines and mAbs. Antiviral drugs have revolutionized the treatment of certain (chronic) viral infections such as those caused by either HIV, HBV, HCV, HSV-1 and HSV-2, and CMV. More recently, antiviral drugs have also become availa- ble against some other viruses including influenza viruses, SARS-CoV-2 and hepatitis delta virus. However, for the majority of the more than 200 known human pathogenic viruses, no antiviral drugs are available. Most of these viruses are RNA viruses — the focus of this Review — including many emerging and clinically important pathogens10–12. Box 1 | Categories and examples of broader-spectrum antivirals (BSAs) for RNA viruses Cross-family BSAs Active against viruses belonging to different (related or unrelated) viral families or across a certain genome architecture (that is, negative-sense single-stranded RNA ((−)ssRNA), positive-sense single-stranded RNA ((+)ssRNA) or double-stranded RNA (dsRNA viruses)), typically by targeting conserved features of the viral replication machinery such as the catalytic site of viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerases. For example, remdesivir, a nucleoside viral polymerase inhibitor, is active against viruses belonging to different viral families, that is, the (−)ssRNA Filoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Pneumoviridae and Arenaviridae as well as the (+) ssRNA Flaviviridae, Picornaviridae and Coronaviridae. Baloxavir, an endonuclease inhibitor, inhibits influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae) but also, although much less potently, several members of the family Peribunyaviridae. Pan-family BSAs Active across all or at least most genera within a single viral family. Examples include neuraminidase inhibitors such as oseltamivir, zanamivir and peramivir that are active against both influenza A and B viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae). Nirmatrelvir is a reversible covalent, peptidomimetic Mpro inhibitor that inhibits human and animal coronaviruses belonging to different genera within the family Coronaviridae. title_original: Towards broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals against RNA viruses

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on rabies virus and rabies disease. It addresses the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, including rabies virus, with the aim of creating antivirals that can target multiple genera, families, or even cross families. The central question is whether such broad-spectrum antivirals can be developed and used effectively for rabies and other RNA viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of antiviral agents active against RNA viruses, including rabies virus. It discusses the rationale for developing BSAs, provides an overview of approved and experimental antivirals, and outlines the biological determinants and clinical development frameworks for these drugs. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria, but it is based on a comprehensive examination of the literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the development of broader-spectrum antivirals is essential to address current unmet medical needs and to strengthen epidemic and pandemic preparedness. It highlights that rabies virus, along with other RNA viruses, is a priority for such antiviral development due to its pandemic potential and broad host range. The review also emphasizes the importance of fixed-dose combinations for treating infections caused by RNA viruses.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that some antivirals, such as azithromycin, itraconazole, and hydroxychloroquine, were rapidly tested in clinical trials with limited preclinical evidence, raising concerns about their efficacy and safety. Additionally, the review highlights that the term 'broad-spectrum' antiviral lacks a clear definition, and there is a need for more precise terminology and criteria. There is also a gap in understanding the mechanisms that underlie the antiviral spectrum of these drugs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that research should focus on developing potent, safe, and orally available antivirals for rabies and other RNA viruses. It also recommends that clinical development frameworks be accelerated, particularly for outbreaks, and that fixed-dose combinations be explored for the treatment of RNA virus infections. Furthermore, it emphasizes the importance of sustained investment in antiviral drug discovery to address both known and emerging viral threats.

analysis.summary_en: This review discusses the development of broader-spectrum direct-acting antivirals (BSAs) against RNA viruses, including rabies virus. It highlights the need for such drugs to address current unmet medical needs and improve pandemic preparedness. The review outlines the rationale for BSAs, provides an overview of existing and experimental antivirals, and emphasizes the importance of fixed-dose combinations. It also notes controversies around the use of certain antivirals with limited evidence and identifies gaps in understanding the mechanisms of antiviral activity. The implications suggest that research should prioritize the development of potent, safe, and orally available antivirals for rabies and other RNA viruses, with accelerated clinical frameworks for outbreaks.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 狂犬病病毒 和 狂犬病 疾病。它解决了针对RNA病毒(包括狂犬病病毒)的更广谱直接作用抗病毒药物(BSA)的开发,旨在创建可以针对多个属、科甚至跨科的抗病毒药物。核心问题是这样的广谱抗病毒药物是否可以开发并有效用于狂犬病和其他RNA病毒。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 抗病毒药物 活性抗 RNA 病毒药物(包括 狂犬病病毒)的系统分析。它讨论了开发 BSA 的基本原理,概述了已批准和实验性的 抗病毒药物,并概述了这些药物的生物决定因素和临床开发框架。该综述没有明确报告数据库、检索日期或资格标准,但它是基于对文献的全面审查。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,开发更广谱的 抗病毒药物 对于解决当前未满足的医疗需求和加强流行病和大流行的防范至关重要。它强调,狂犬病病毒 与其他 RNA 病毒一样,由于其大流行潜力和广泛的 宿主 范围,是 抗病毒药物 开发的优先事项。该综述还强调了固定剂量组合治疗 RNA 病毒引起的感染的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,一些 抗病毒药物,如阿奇霉素、伊曲康唑和羟氯喹,在临床前证据有限的情况下迅速进行了临床试验,引发了对其有效性和安全性的担忧。此外,审查还强调,“广谱”抗病毒药物 一词缺乏明确的定义,需要更精确的术语和标准。对这些药物 抗病毒药物 谱背后的机制的理解也存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查建议研究应集中于开发针对 狂犬病 和其他 RNA 病毒的有效、安全且口服的 抗病毒药物。它还建议加快临床开发框架,特别是暴发,并探索针对RNA病毒感染的治疗的固定剂量组合。此外,它还强调了持续投资 抗病毒药物 药物发现以应对已知和新出现的病毒威胁的重要性。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,开发更广谱的 抗病毒药物 对于解决当前未满足的医疗需求和加强流行病和大流行的防范至关重要。它强调,狂犬病病毒 与其他 RNA 病毒一样,由于其大流行潜力和广泛的 宿主 范围,是 抗病毒药物 开发的优先事项。该综述还强调了固定剂量组合治疗 RNA 病毒引起的感染的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,一些 抗病毒药物,如阿奇霉素、伊曲康唑和羟氯喹,在临床前证据有限的情况下迅速进行了临床试验,引发了对其有效性和安全性的担忧。此外,审查还强调,“广谱”抗病毒药物 一词缺乏明确的定义,需要更精确的术语和标准。对这些药物 抗病毒药物 谱背后的机制的理解也存在差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查建议研究应集中于开发针对 狂犬病 和其他 RNA 病毒的有效、安全且口服的 抗病毒药物。它还建议加快临床开发框架,特别是暴发,并探索针对RNA病毒感染的治疗的固定剂量组合。此外,它还强调了持续投资 抗病毒药物 药物发现以应对已知和新出现的病毒威胁的重要性。

full_text: AbstractFor nearly 50 years, scientists have sought to exploit messenger RNA (mRNA) as a therapeutic tool, overcoming major challenges related to instability, delivery, and inflammatory reactions. A major breakthrough came with the incorporation of modified nucleosides, particularly pseudouridine, during in vitro mRNA synthesis, which markedly improved stability, translation efficiency, and tolerability. The clinical success of mRNA technology was demonstrated in 2020 with the development of highly effective and safe COVID-19 vaccines, administered to over a billion individuals worldwide. These achievements inaugurated a new era in molecular medicine. In this review, we revisit the historical development of mRNA delivery into human cells and discuss the emergence of mRNA as a gene-therapy approach. In fact, beyond vaccination, mRNA platforms are rapidly expanding toward protein replacement therapies for genetic disorders and innovative strategies for cancer treatment. We summarize advances in synthetic mRNA design and optimization, delivery vehicles, and administration strategies that enable therapeutic applications. Finally, we highlight current limitations, technological challenges, and future opportunities, emphasizing how mRNA-based technologies have become powerful tools for studying gene function and developing next-generation precision therapies. IntroductionSince the discovery of the RNA functions as information messenger, scientists have worked extensively to understand how mRNA could be used to treat human diseases. These efforts faced many challenges until 2008, when Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman made the fundamental discovery indicating that the incorporation of modified nucleosides into the mRNA molecules (particularly N1-methylpseudouridine and 5-methylcytidine) could overcome exacerbated inflammatory reactions and, together with the development of lipid nanoparticles as a delivery system, rendered these molecules therapeutically viable (Karikó et al., 2005, 2008). In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the approval of the first mRNA-based vaccines for human use represented a major milestone, highlighting the therapeutic potential of mRNA technology. The vaccination of more than one billion individuals worldwide demonstrated not only high efficacy in protecting humans against specific viral pathogens but also demonstrated the safety and feasibility of using mRNA molecules for broader biomedical applications, including therapies for human genetic and acquired diseases. mRNA-based therapeutics offer several advantages, including the absence of genomic integration, high versatility, and rapid development and production. However, as with any other therapeutic strategy, important challenges remain, particularly regarding cell- and tissue-specific delivery and precise modulation of the immune system (Wei et al., 2023). This review focuses on recent advances in the use of mRNA molecules as potential gene therapy tools, highlights current strategies and future perspectives. The application of mRNA molecules as vaccines against cancer is also summarized. In contrast, mRNA vaccines for infectious diseases are addressed primarily from a historical perspective, emphasizing key discoveries related to the delivery of these molecules to cells and organisms. Readers interested in recent developments in vaccines for infectious diseases or cancer are encouraged to consult comprehensive and up-to-date reviews on the topic (Ali, 2025; Quan et al., 2025). The history of mRNA delivery systemsThe messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) was first described in 1961 by François Gros and colleagues (Gros et al., 1961). Seventeen years later, in 1978, mRNA was successfully transfected into cells, when mRNA encoding a globin-like protein was delivered into human epithelial carcinoma (HEp-2) cells using liposomes, resulting in detectable protein translation (Ostro et al., 1978). Subsequently, in vitro synthesis of mRNA encoding Xenopus β-globin using SP6 bacteriophage RNA polymerase was achieved from complementary DNA (cDNA). Injection of these mRNA molecules into frog oocyte cytoplasm resulted in efficient protein translation. Importantly, this process was shown to depend on the presence of 5’cap modification, whereas deletion of most of the 3’ flanking region, including the poly(A) tail, did not completely abolish protein synthesis (Krieg and Melton, 1984). Further advances demonstrated that in vitro-transcribed (IVT) luciferase mRNA could be introduced into NIH 3T3 mouse cells using a lipid-based delivery system, leading to measurable luciferase activity (Malone et al., 1989). Shortly thereafter, direct injection of IVT mRNA (encoding chloramphenicol acetyltransferase, luciferase, and beta-galactosidase) into the skeletal muscle of mice also resulted in successful in vivo protein expression (Wolff et al., 1990). Despite these early breakthroughs, progress in mRNA-based therapeutics remained limited for many years due to significant technical challenges, including liability and strong endogenous inflammatory reactions (Sahin et al., 2014).Building upon these early advances, the pioneer experiments for mRNA therapy were reported in 1992 using Brattleboro rats, a strain that served as a model for diabetes insipidus, due to the inability to produce the hormone vasopressin. Direct intracerebral injection of vasopressin-encoding mRNA restored hormone production and effectively reversed disease symptoms within hours, with therapeutic effects lasting up to five days after treatment (Jirikowski et al., 1992). This study provided one of the earliest proofs of concept that exogenous mRNA could be used to transiently replace defective or absent proteins in vivo.Parallel efforts explored the potential of mRNA as a vaccination platform. In 1993, the IVT influenza virus nucleoprotein mRNA encapsulated into liposomes was shown to induce a robust immune response in mice, stimulating the production of cytotoxic T lymphocytes, essential for eliminating virus-infected cells (Martinon et al., 1993). These findings highlighted the capacity of mRNA to stimulate antigen-specific cellular immunity and suggested its potential application in infectious disease prevention.Shortly thereafter, the feasibility of mRNA-based cancer vaccines was demonstrated. A capped, polyadenylated, and stabilized mRNA encoding a tumor-associated carcinoembryonic antigen was delivered into mouse fibroblast cells via liposome-mediated transfection, resulting in efficient antigen expression. In pilot in vivo experiments, immunization with this mRNA triggered antigen-specific immune responses and protected mice from colon carcinoma cells engineered to express the same antigen (Conry et al., 1995). These results provided early evidence that mRNA vaccination could generate protective antitumor immunity.Together, these pioneering studies established the conceptual and experimental foundations for mRNA-based therapeutics and vaccination, although widespread application remained limited by technical challenges related to mRNA stability, delivery efficiency, and exacerbated inflammation.Concurrently, several post-transcriptional nucleoside modifications in RNA were identified, such as the deamination of adenosines and cytidines, which were shown to influence mRNA translation efficiency and regulation (Kiss, 2001). Numerous modified ribonucleotides were subsequently described for the major cellular RNA classes, including tRNAs, rRNAs, mRNA, and snRNAs, most of which are introduced post-transcriptionally (Limbach et al., 1994; Kiss, 2001). These modifications were demonstrated to play essential structural and functional roles. In tRNAs, for example, nucleotide modifications promote accurate anticodon-codon pairing and enhance both the efficiency and fidelity of translation (Agris, 1996; Kiss, 2001).In the early 2000s, fundamental discoveries in understanding mRNA inflammatory reactions emerged from studies of Karikó and Weissman. Their work demonstrated that IVT RNA molecules activate human Toll-like receptor (TLR) 3, thereby triggering innate immune responses (Karikó et al., 2004). Similarly, bacterial RNA was also shown to stimulate innate immunity and inflammation, while mRNA and tRNA derived from eukaryotic sources failed to activate cultured human dendritic cells (DC) (Koski et al., 2004). TLRs are key initiators of adaptive immune responses, promoting T-cell differentiation into T helper 1 effector cells against microbial infections through recognition of foreign nucleic acids (Medzhitov, 2001). Importantly, activation of these receptors by exogenous mRNA significantly limits protein expression due to cell death following cellular transfection, representing a major obstacle for therapeutic applications. Subsequent studies by Karikó and Weissman led to a seminal discovery demonstrating that the incorporation of modified nucleosides-including 5-methylcytidine (m5C), N6-methyladenosine (m6A), 5-methyluridine (m5U), 2-thiouridine (s2U), and pseudouridine-during in vitro mRNA synthesis markedly suppresses TLR-mediated inflammatory reactions (Karikó et al., 2005). Their work furthermore showed that mitochondrial RNA (mtRNA) stimulates monocyte-derived dendritic cells (MDDCs), whereas mammalian tRNA did not induce detectable levels of tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α). This difference is likely explained by the structural similarity between mitochondrial and bacterial RNA, both of which contain relatively few nucleoside modifications and therefore act as potent DC activators. In contrast, tRNAs are highly modified and show little or no activity of DC activation (Karikó et al., 2005). Further advances demonstrated that mRNA containing pseudouridine exhibits significantly enhanced translational capacity compared to unmodified transcripts, when introduced in mammalian cells, cell-free lysates, or following intravenous administration into mice. Importantly, only unmodified mRNA induced strong immunogenic responses, including high levels of interferon alpha production (Karikó et al., 2008). In Figure 1, a historical timeline for these discoveries, which turned possible the use of mRNA for vaccine and therapy, is presented.Collectively, these findings established that incorporation of modified nucleosides, particularly pseudouridine, during in vitro mRNA synthesis was critical for reducing innate immune recognition, cell death and activation of deleterious inflammatory responses, which resulted in enhanced expression of proteins encoded by the exogenous mRNA and, thereby, enabling the development of effective therapeutic mRNA platforms. Figure 2 illustrates the biological outcomes of transfection with RNA molecules synthesized with pseudouridine, namely elimination of innate inflammatory responses, and improvement of translation efficiency. Figure 1 - The timeline history of mRNA gene therapy. Figure 2 - Representative scheme of the biological outcome of uridine substitution with pseudouridine. Replacement of uridine with pseudouridine during in vitro mRNA synthesis provides significant advantages when the mRNA is introduced into cells. These benefits include higher translational efficiency, leading to increased protein production, as well as a reduced inflammatory response. Figure adapted from the Nobel Prize announcement website. https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2023/advanced-information/. As a consequence of the landmark discoveries made by Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman, along with their broader outstanding contributions to the development of nucleoside-modified mRNA technology, they were awarded the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2023/). Their work was fundamental by enabling the development of effective mRNA vaccines, including those used against COVID-19. The first-in-human clinical trial for an mRNA vaccine encoding the rabies virus glycoprotein (CV7201) was conducted before any signs of the COVID-19 pandemic and published in 2017 (Alberer et al., 2017). In this study, female and male volunteers with no prior history of rabies vaccination received escalating doses administered intradermally or intramuscularly using needle-syringe or needle-free devices, followed by a booster dose after one year. This trial represented the first demonstration of an effective mRNA-based vaccine tested in humans. The vaccine successfully induced antibody responses against the viral antigen and proved to be safe and well-tolerated (Alberer et al., 2017). Of note, in 2018, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based therapy carrying a small interfering RNA (siRNA) (patisiran, Onpattro®) (Akinc et al., 2019). This drug, indicated for the treatment of polyneuropathy associated with hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults, inhibits the hepatic synthesis of transthyretin (mutant and wild-type). It acts by specifically binding to a genetically conserved sequence in the 3’ untranslated region of transthyretin messenger RNA (Hoy, 2018). This approval marked the first regulatory validation of an LNP system designed to deliver an RNA molecule in humans and demonstrated that such platforms could safely and effectively enable systemic nucleic acid delivery. Indeed, incorporation of the mRNA molecules into ionizable LNPs conferred both increased stability to the molecules and, simultaneously, offer a highly efficient approach to introduce mRNA molecules into the cytoplasm of transfected cells. These advances were critical for clinical translation and later supported the development and approval of mRNA-based vaccines for human use. In December 2020, the biotech companies Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna received emergency use authorization for the COVID-19 mRNA-based vaccines from the U.S. FDA and from the European Medicines Agency (EMA). In both vaccines, the nucleoside-modified mRNA encoding the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein is administered intramuscularly using lipid nanoparticle-formulation. These groundbreaking vaccines played a pivotal role in mitigating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Their rapid development, high efficacy, and adaptability to emerging viral variants established a new paradigm for vaccine design and highlighted the potential of mRNA platforms for combating future infectious diseases and other medical conditions (Lamb, 2021). mRNA-based therapy for protein replacement Several human genetic disorders result from mutations leading to deficiencies in the activity or the production of specific enzymes. A transformative therapeutic strategy for many of these conditions has been enzyme replacement therapy (ERT), which involves the application of recombinant forms of the missing enzyme to patients, with important clinical benefits. However, ERT presents several limitations, including reactogenicity, limited penetration into the central nervous system, and variable transfection efficacy for skeletal muscle. In addition, the high costs of the treatment substantially restricted its widespread clinical use (Choi et al., 2025).Following the demonstrated success and safety of mRNA-based vaccines, the therapeutic use of mRNA that efficiently expresses the deficient enzyme has emerged as a promising alternative for the treatment of certain genetic disorders. Thus, the mRNA-based protein replacement represents an innovative strategy in which synthetic IVT mRNA is delivered to the patient cells to direct the synthesis of functional therapeutic proteins employing the host cellular translational machinery (Żak and Zangi, 2025). This approach offers potential advantages, including transient protein expression, avoidance of genomic integration, and flexible manufacturing. In this section, key studies of mRNA-based therapeutics for genetic disorders are presented.Considering hematological diseases, hemophilia A and hemophilia B are caused by deficiencies in factors VIII and IX, respectively (Sidonio and Malec, 2021). Preclinical studies evaluating mRNA-based therapies have been conducted to explore treatments for those disorders. For hemophilia B, an mRNA-drug encapsulated in LUNAR lipid nanoparticles (LNPs; LUNAR- a proprietary mRNA delivery platform developed by Arcturus Therapeutics, San Diego, CA, USA) encoding human factor IX (hFIX) was administered in immunocompetent hemophilic mice. High circulation levels of hFIX protein were detected after repeated administrations, demonstrating sustained protein expression (Ramaswamy et al., 2017). Similarly, studies investigating mRNA-based therapy for hemophilia A demonstrated that intravenous injection of LNP encapsulated luciferase mRNA, resulted in detectable hepatic luminescence within four hours, with no toxicity even after multiple administrations. Based on these findings, the mRNA encoding factor VIII protein was subsequently evaluated (Chen et al., 2020). This approach successfully restored biological activity, and production of therapeutic factor VIII (FVIII) protein levels was detected, above therapeutic levels, over five days. Repeated injections of FVIII-mRNA prolonged the duration of FVIII expression (Chen et al., 2020). The Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency (OTCD) is an X-linked genetic disorder, characterized by severe disease onset during the neonatal period, most frequently in males, although the post-neonatal manifestations may occur in both sexes (Lichter-Konecki et al., 2022). OTC is a key enzyme in the urea cycle, a metabolic pathway responsible for ammonia detoxification. Deficiency of OTC leads to an ammonia build up in the blood (hyperammonemia), which is neurotoxic in affected individuals. To address these disorders, LNP formulations encapsulating OTC mRNA have been developed as a hepatocyte-targeted delivery system for OTC intracellular enzyme replacement therapy.
